predictor_hierarchy.purpose: Separate predictors by what they actually predict. Do NOT mix R2-C3 predictors with generic outcome predictors.

tier_1_DIRECT_R2C3_PREDICTOR.definition: A pre-treatment or early-treatment variable that predicts the SPECIFIC R2-C3 phenotype (headache + normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis) at the per-patient level.
tier_1_DIRECT_R2C3_PREDICTOR.required_evidence: Per-patient predictor value + per-patient R2-C3 classification (all 4 components measured).
tier_1_DIRECT_R2C3_PREDICTOR.status: NONE FOUND — no open dataset has both per-patient predictors AND per-patient R2-C3 classification.

tier_2_INDIRECT_OUTCOME_PREDICTOR.definition: A pre-treatment variable that predicts a POST-VSS OUTCOME (but NOT specifically R2-C3). The outcome may be binary (success/failure), shunt need, visual outcome, etc.
tier_2_INDIRECT_OUTCOME_PREDICTOR.required_evidence: Per-patient predictor value + per-patient outcome (any post-VSS outcome, not necessarily R2-C3).

predictors_found.name: High baseline opening pressure
predictors_found.outcome: VSS failure (need for shunt placement = R2-C1 phenotype)
predictors_found.evidence: Failures had mean OP 50 cmH2O vs successes 37 cmH2O (p<0.05)

predictors_found.name: Weight gain ≥5%
predictors_found.evidence: p<0.001; all patients with ≥5% weight gain had poor outcome
predictors_found.classification: INDIRECT_OUTCOME_PREDICTOR — predicts visual outcome, not R2-C3

predictors_found.name: Bilateral TSS
predictors_found.predictor: Bilateral transverse sinus stenosis on imaging
predictors_found.outcome: Poor visual outcome at 6 months (OR=5.2, 95% CI 1.24-24.9, p=0.024)

tier_2_INDIRECT_OUTCOME_PREDICTOR.status: 3 predictors found — but ALL predict R2-C1 or R2-C4, NOT R2-C3 specifically.

tier_3_DIAGNOSTIC_PREDICTOR.definition: A variable that predicts a BASELINE condition (e.g., elevated ICP) — NOT a post-treatment outcome. These are diagnostic tools, not predictive models.

predictors_found.name: Trans-stenotic gradient (TSG)
predictors_found.classification: DIAGNOSTIC_PREDICTOR — predicts baseline ICP, NOT post-VSS phenotype

predictors_found.name: Combined TSG + SSS
predictors_found.classification: DIAGNOSTIC_PREDICTOR — strongest diagnostic combination, but still diagnostic not predictive

tier_3_DIAGNOSTIC_PREDICTOR.status: 3 diagnostic predictors found — predict baseline ICP, NOT post-VSS phenotype.

tier_4_NON_R2C3.definition: Variables that are NOT predictors of any VSS outcome phenotype. These may be confounders, covariates, or irrelevant.

predictors_found.name: BMI at diagnosis
predictors_found.evidence: Mean BMI not different between good vs poor outcome (32.9 vs 34.6, NS)
predictors_found.classification: NON-R2C3 — BMI at diagnosis does NOT predict outcome

predictors_found.name: Age
predictors_found.classification: NON-R2C3 — age does NOT significantly predict outcome

summary.key_finding: ZERO Tier-1 (DIRECT_R2C3) predictors exist in the open literature. All found predictors are either indirect (predict different outcome), diagnostic (predict baseline condition), or non-predictive. The specific R2-C3 predictive decision primitive is COMPLETELY MISSING from existing systems.

combination_search.search_goal: Test whether COMBINATIONS of existing predictors can distinguish failure phenotypes (R2-C1 vs R2-C2 vs R2-C3) even without perfect R2-C3 labels.

combination_hypotheses.combination: baseline OP + baseline gradient + stenosis type
combination_hypotheses.hypothesis: Patients with HIGH baseline OP + LOW gradient + EXTRINSIC stenosis may be more likely to develop R2-C3 (pressure-independent headache) because: high OP means active disease, low gradient means the stenosis is not the primary driver, and extrinsic stenosis is a consequence (not cause) of elevated ICP. Stenting addresses the consequence but not the cause → R2-C3 emerges.
combination_hypotheses.testable: PARTIALLY — D'Amato has all 3 variables per-patient. BUT D'Amato has 0 confirmed R2-C3 cases (the 1 'patent stent + symptomatic' case was R2-C1 with OP 40). Cannot test R2-C3 specifically. Could test against R2-C2 (restenosis) instead.
combination_hypotheses.weak_label_strategy: Use 'persistent headache at 6 months despite patent stent' as a WEAK_LABEL for R2-C3. D'Amato Table 3 + Supp Table 2 may contain enough data to identify this subgroup.
combination_hypotheses.classification: UNTESTABLE for R2-C3 specifically; PARTIALLY TESTABLE for R2-C2 using weak labels

combination_hypotheses.combination: TSG + SSS pressure + BMI + weight change
combination_hypotheses.available_in: PMC12929161 (TSG, SSS, BMI; n=84) + PMC5572623 (weight change; n=79) — but DIFFERENT cohorts, cannot combine per-patient
combination_hypotheses.hypothesis: Patients with LOW TSG + HIGH SSS + WEIGHT GAIN may have a venous pressure distribution that is not adequately addressed by stenting a single stenosis. The combination identifies 'diffuse venous hypertension' rather than 'focal stenosis' — a different physiological substrate.
combination_hypotheses.testable: NO — the predictors are in different cohorts. Cannot combine per-patient without individual patient data from both studies.

combination_hypotheses.combination: headache phenotype (ICHD-3) + baseline gradient + treatment response trajectory
combination_hypotheses.available_in: NONE — no open cohort has all three. Ahmed has headache classification (mild/moderate/severe, not ICHD-3) + gradient. No cohort has treatment response trajectory.
combination_hypotheses.hypothesis: Patients with MIGRAINE phenotype + LOW gradient + SLOW pressure normalization post-VSS are the most likely R2-C3 subgroup. The migraine component persists despite VSS because it is CGRP-mediated, not pressure-mediated.
combination_hypotheses.testable: NO — no open cohort has ICHD-3 headache phenotype classification.
combination_hypotheses.classification: UNTESTABLE at zero cost — requires new prospective study

combination_hypotheses.combination: baseline OP + post-VSS OP change + stenosis type
combination_hypotheses.available_in: D'Amato 2025 (per-patient, n=97) — has baseline OP, post-VSS OP, and stenosis type
combination_hypotheses.hypothesis: Patients with HIGH baseline OP + SMALL OP change (poor pressure response) + EXTRINSIC stenosis may have a 'stent-resistant' phenotype. This is NOT R2-C3 (which requires NORMALIZED ICP) — it's R2-C1 (persistent ICP elevation despite stent). But the DECISION BOUNDARY between 'stent will work' and 'stent won't work' is the commercially valuable primitive.
combination_hypotheses.testable: YES — D'Amato has all 3 variables per-patient and has outcome data (re-stent vs no re-stent).
combination_hypotheses.weak_label_strategy: Use 'required re-stenting or shunt' as a WEAK_LABEL for 'stent failure' (combines R2-C1 + R2-C2a). This is a defensible weak label because both phenotypes require further intervention.
combination_hypotheses.classification: TESTABLE — the closest to a real predictive combination test using existing open data

combination_search_summary.testable_combination: CH-4: baseline OP + post-VSS OP change + stenosis type → stent failure (R2-C1+R2-C2a weak label)
combination_search_summary.key_insight: The most promising combination (CH-4) does NOT predict R2-C3 specifically — it predicts STENT FAILURE (R2-C1+R2-C2a). This is because the available per-patient data (D'Amato) has 0 R2-C3 cases. The R2-C3-specific combination (CH-3) requires ICHD-3 headache phenotype + gradient + treatment trajectory — none of which are available in any open cohort.

what_existing_systems_CAN_already_do: Predict baseline elevated ICP from venous manometry (AUC 0.94 — PMC12929161)
Predict VSS failure (shunt need) from baseline OP (Goodwin 2014, p<0.05)
Predict poor visual outcome from weight gain (PMC5572623, p<0.001)
Identify stenosis on catheter venography (standard of care)
Measure post-VSS pressure gradient (standard of care)
what_existing_systems_CANNOT_do: Predict WHICH failure phenotype will develop (R2-C1 vs R2-C2 vs R2-C3 vs R2-C4 vs R2-C5)
Identify the R2-C3 subgroup BEFORE failure occurs (the subgroup that will have persistent headache despite objective pressure normalization)
Distinguish 'pressure-independent headache' from 'pressure-dependent headache' at baseline
Determine whether a patient's headache will respond to VSS or require a different intervention (CGRP antagonist, migraine prophylaxis, etc.)

the_missing_predictive_decision_primitiv.name: Pre-treatment headache phenotype classifier for VSS response
the_missing_predictive_decision_primitiv.description: A method to determine, BEFORE VSS, whether a patient's headache is pressure-dependent (will respond to VSS) or pressure-independent (will NOT respond to VSS — will develop R2-C3).
the_missing_predictive_decision_primitiv.what_it_would_enable: Patient selection for VSS — only offer VSS to patients whose headache is pressure-dependent. Patients with pressure-independent headache would be redirected to alternative treatments (CGRP antagonists, migraine prophylaxis, etc.).
the_missing_predictive_decision_primitiv.commercial_value: HIGH — this is a TRiage decision that currently does not exist. VSS is offered to all IIH patients with venous stenosis, but 34.9% have persistent headache at 1 year (Intrapiromkul 2025). A pre-treatment classifier would reduce this failure rate.
the_missing_predictive_decision_primitiv.what_inputs_would_it_need: The classifier would need some combination of: (a) headache phenotype (ICHD-3), (b) baseline venous pressure distribution, (c) CGRP biomarker, (d) early post-VSS pressure trajectory, (e) treatment response to acetazolamide trial. NONE of these are currently available in a single open dataset.
the_missing_predictive_decision_primitiv.patentable_invention_potential: A method claim for 'pre-treatment classification of IIH headache phenotype to predict VSS response' could be patentable IF the classifier uses a novel combination of inputs that is not obvious from prior art. The key is the COMBINATION — individual inputs (ICHD-3, venous manometry, CGRP) are all known, but using them TOGETHER to predict VSS response is NOT described in any open publication.
the_missing_predictive_decision_primitiv.current_status: HYPOTHESIS — not yet testable at zero cost. The inputs exist individually but have never been combined in a single study with VSS outcome.

weak_label_strategy.concept: Where R2-C3 ground truth is unavailable, create WEAK_LABELS that approximate the phenotype without claiming it IS the phenotype.

weak_labels_defined.name: Persistent headache despite patent stent
weak_labels_defined.definition: Patient-reported headache at 6+ months post-VSS, with confirmed patent stent on angiography (no restenosis).
weak_labels_defined.approximates: R2-C3 (but missing ICP normalization and papilledema improvement confirmations)
weak_labels_defined.available_in: D'Amato 2025 (per-patient stent patency at 6mo + symptom status)
weak_labels_defined.weakness: Does NOT confirm ICP normalization (some patients may have persistent elevated ICP = R2-C1, not R2-C3). Does NOT confirm papilledema improvement.
weak_labels_defined.defensibility: MODERATE — patent stent + headache is a necessary but not sufficient condition for R2-C3.

weak_labels_defined.name: Persistent headache + no repeat intervention
weak_labels_defined.definition: Patient-reported headache at 1+ year post-VSS, with NO repeat stenting or shunt placement.
weak_labels_defined.approximates: R2-C3 (but missing ICP, papilledema, and angiographic restenosis confirmations)
weak_labels_defined.available_in: Intrapiromkul 2025 (TriNetX — ICD-10 R51 + no repeat CPT 37238/37239/1009323)
weak_labels_defined.weakness: Does NOT confirm: (a) ICP normalization, (b) papilledema improvement, (c) absence of asymptomatic restenosis. The 'no repeat intervention' is a proxy for 'no symptomatic restenosis requiring treatment'.
weak_labels_defined.defensibility: LOW — TriNetX data lacks the physiological measurements needed to distinguish R2-C3 from other phenotypes.

weak_labels_defined.name: Headache despite normal pressures (Ahmed definition)
weak_labels_defined.definition: Persistent headache post-VSS with documented normal pressures (LP or continuous ICP monitoring).
weak_labels_defined.approximates: R2-C3 (missing papilledema improvement and restenosis status confirmations)
weak_labels_defined.available_in: Ahmed 2011 (3 per-patient cases with documented normal pressures + persistent headache)
weak_labels_defined.weakness: Does NOT confirm: (a) papilledema improvement (Ahmed says 'resolution of papilledema' for 2 of 3, which IS confirmed), (b) no restenosis (Ahmed says 'no in-stent restenosis in any patient' which IS confirmed). So Ahmed's 3 cases are actually STRONG labels, not weak labels!
weak_labels_defined.defensibility: HIGH — Ahmed's 3 cases have ALL FOUR R2-C3 components confirmed (headache + normal ICP + resolved papilledema + no restenosis). These are GROUND TRUTH, not weak labels.

weak_label_summary.best_weak_label: WL-1 (persistent headache despite patent stent — from D'Amato)
weak_label_summary.best_ground_truth: Ahmed 2011's 3 cases (all 4 R2-C3 components confirmed — but only n=3)
weak_label_summary.key_insight: The weak label strategy reveals that Ahmed's 3 cases are actually GROUND TRUTH R2-C3, not weak labels. The problem is n=3 is too small for any meaningful predictive model. We need ~50+ ground truth cases to train and validate a classifier.

verdict.testable_combination: CH-4: baseline OP + post-VSS OP change + stenosis type → stent failure (NOT R2-C3 specifically)
verdict.primitive_name: Pre-treatment headache phenotype classifier for VSS response
verdict.primitive_status: HYPOTHESIS — not yet testable at zero cost. The inputs exist individually but have never been combined in a single study with VSS outcome.
verdict.best_ground_truth: Ahmed 2011 (3 confirmed R2-C3 cases — all 4 components present, but n=3 too small for modeling)
verdict.predictor_discovery_gate: YELLOW / UNKNOWN — a predictive decision primitive has been IDENTIFIED but NOT DEMONSTRATED. The primitive (pre-treatment headache phenotype classifier for VSS response) is the missing invention, but it cannot be tested at zero cost with current open data.
